rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction omits a possessive noun: the question is whether the idols hear your invocation.
rows.anchor: لا بد في { يسمعونكم } من تقدير حذف المضاف ، معناه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda reads it as asking whether the idols hear the response to the invocation and can answer.
rows.anchor: وقرأ قتادة : ( يسمعونكم ) ، أي : هل يسمعونكم الجواب عن دعائكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present-tense verb appears with past-time إذ to portray the past situation as ongoing.
rows.anchor: وجاء مضارعا مع إيقاعه في إذ على حكاية الحال الماضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recreating the past makes the hearers recall each invocation and ask whether the idols ever heard or answered, sharpening the rebuke.
rows.anchor: استحضروا الأحوال الماضية التي كنتم تدعونها فيها ، وقولوا هل سمعوا أو أسمعوا قط .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrahim pushes their appeal to inherited practice to its oldest ancestors: precedence proves nothing, and falsehood does not become true through age.
rows.anchor: لما أجابوه بجواب المقلدين لآبائهم قال لهم : رقوا أمر تقليدكم هذا إلى أقصى غاياته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worshipping idols is worship of enemies: the idols will repudiate their worshippers, and Satan, who induces the worship, is humanity's greatest enemy.
rows.anchor: وما عبادة من عبد هذه الأصنام إلا عبادة أعداء له ، ومعنى العداوة قوله تعالى : { كلا سيكفرون بعبادتهم ويكونون عليهم ضدا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrahim frames the conclusion as advice he first gave himself, presenting his reasoning as sincere counsel and inviting his audience to accept it through reflection.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال : { عدو لى } تصويرا للمسألة في نفسه ، على معنى : أني فكرت في أمرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Enemy and friend can each take singular or collective meaning; Zamakhshari cites poetry and 18:50 as examples.
rows.anchor: والعدو والصديق : يجيئان في معنى الوحدة والجماعة .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is disconnected, with the sense: rather, the Lord of the worlds.
rows.anchor: استثناء منقطع ، كأنه قال : ولكن رب العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After creating Ibrahim and breathing life into him, God continuously guides him toward what benefits him, including nourishment and the skills of infancy.
rows.anchor: فهو يهدين } يريد أنه حين أتم خلقه ونفخ فيه الروح ، عقب ذلك هدايته المتصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrahim attributes illness to himself rather than saying God made him ill because people often bring sickness on themselves through careless eating and drinking; philosophers blamed indigestion for many deaths.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال : { مرضات } دون ( أمرضني ) لأن كثيرا من أسباب المرض يحدث بتفريط من الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads the plural خطاياي; Zamakhshari takes the requested forgiveness as covering occasional minor slips.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( خطاياي ) ، والمراد : ما يندر منه من بعض الصغائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The slips are minor, since prophets are protected and chosen above the worlds.
rows.anchor: والمراد : ما يندر منه من بعض الصغائر ؛ لأن الأنبياء معصومون مختارون على العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed view identifies the errors as Ibrahim's statements that he was ill, that the largest idol did it, and that Sarah was his sister.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هي قوله : { إنى سقيم } ( الصافات : 89 ) وقوله : { بل فعله كبيرهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zamakhshari rejects calling those statements sins: they are indirect expressions and stratagems addressed to unbelievers, not offenses requiring forgiveness.
rows.anchor: وما هي إلا معاريض كلام ، وتخييلات للكفرة ، وليست بخطايا يطلب لها الاستغفار .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophetic requests for forgiveness express humility and self-abasement, teach their communities to avoid sin and seek pardon, and offer hope rather than a categorical claim.
rows.anchor: أن استغفار الأنبياء تواضع منهم لربهم ، وهضم لأنفسهم ، ويدل عليه قوله : { أطمع }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgiveness is attached to Judgment Day because the consequences of the sin become visible then, though hidden now.
rows.anchor: لأن أثرها يتبين يومئذ وهو الآن خفي لا يعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God seized them with the cloud punishment they had demanded if they meant a cloud; if they meant a canopy, the punishment contradicted their request.
rows.anchor: {فأخذهم } الله بنحو ما اقترحوا من عذاب الظلة إن أرادوا بالسماء السحاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says wind was withheld for seven days and suffocating heat drove them into the open; a cool cloud gathered them beneath it, then rained fire and burned them.
rows.anchor: يروى أنه حبس عنهم الريح سبعا ، وسلط عليهم الومد . فأخذ بأنفاسهم لا ينفعهم ظل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says Shuayb was sent to Midian and the People of the Thicket: Gabriel's cry destroyed Midian, while the latter received the cloud punishment.
rows.anchor: وروي أن شعيبا بعث إلى أمتين : أصحاب مدين ، وأصحاب الأيكة ، فأهلكت مدين بصيحة جبريل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each repeated story is like a self-contained revelation and merits the same opening and conclusion because each carries its own lesson.
rows.anchor: كل قصة منها كتنزيل برأسه ، وفيها من الاعتبار مثل ما في غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repetition fixes meanings in the soul and memory: repeated review strengthens understanding and makes knowledge harder to forget.
rows.anchor: ولأن في التكرير تقريرا للمعاني في الأنفس ، وتثبيتا لها في الصدور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stories are repeated because listeners are deaf to truth and hearts closed to reflection; reiteration may open ears and minds and polish understanding dulled by neglect.
rows.anchor: ولأن هذه القصص طرقت بها آذان وقر عن الإنصات للحق ، وقلوب غلف عن تدبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is given to Muhammad and taught to him by God.
rows.anchor: { لتلقى القرءان } لتؤتاه وتلقنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite forms magnify the wisdom and knowledge of the one from whom the Qur'an comes.
rows.anchor: { من لدن حكيم عليم } عند أي { حكيم } وأي { عليم } وهذا معنى مجيئهما نكرتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse prepares for the ensuing narratives, which display the subtleties of God's wisdom and the intricacies of His knowledge.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية بساط وتمهيد ، لما يريد أن يسوق بعدها من الأقاصيص وما في ذلك من لطائف حكمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word describes Moses watching for someone to confront him on the road or catch up with him.
rows.anchor: {يترقب } التعرض له في الطريق . أو أن يلحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tلقاء means toward; Midian is Shuayb's village, named for Midyan son of Abraham, outside Pharaoh's rule and eight days from Egypt.
rows.anchor: { تلقاء مدين } قصدها ونحوها . ومدين : قرية شعيب عليه السلام ، سميت بمدين بن إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Midian was not under Pharaoh's authority and lay an eight-day journey from Egypt.
rows.anchor: ولم تكن في سلطان فرعون ، وبينها وبين مصر مسيرة ثمان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses left without knowing the route, relying only on his good expectation of God.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : خرج وليس له علم بالطريق إلا حسن ظنه بربه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight way is its middle and the main course of the route.
rows.anchor: و { سواء السبيل } وسطه ومعظم نهجه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed report says Moses went barefoot, lived on leaves, and wore away the sole of a foot before arriving.
rows.anchor: وقيل : خرج حافيا لا يعيش إلا بورق الشجر ، فما وصل حتى سقط خف قدمه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says an angel on horseback, carrying a spear, guided Moses to Midian.
rows.anchor: وقيل : جاءه ملك على فرس بيده عنزة ، فانطلق به إلى مدين .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water of Midian was the source from which its people drew; reports identify it as a well.
rows.anchor: { ماء مدين } ماءهم الذي يستقون منه ، وكان بئرا فيما روي .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wurud means coming to and reaching the water.
rows.anchor: ووروده : مجيئه والوصول إليه { وجد عليه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He found the people above the well, at its rim and watering place.
rows.anchor: { وجد عليه } وجد فوق شفيره ومستقاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The group is a large crowd, and its people are drawn from different communities.
rows.anchor: { أمة } جماعة كثيفة العدد { من الناس } من أناس مختلفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two women were at a lower place than the crowd.
rows.anchor: { من دونهم } في مكان أسفل من مكانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb means driving away or pushing back; they held their flock back because the men at the water were stronger and prevented them from drawing.
rows.anchor: والذود : الطرد والدفع وإنما كانتا تذودان ؛ لأن على الماء من هو أقوى منهما فلا يتمكنان من السقي .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations say the women avoided crowding, kept their sheep apart from the men's flocks, or shielded their faces from onlookers.
rows.anchor: كانتا تكرهان المزاحمة على الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks their situation; literally it asks what they seek, with خطب deriving from a sought matter, as شأن derives from intending a purpose.
rows.anchor: { ما خطبكما } ما شأنكما . وحقيقته : ما مخطوبكما ، أي : مطلوبكما من الزياد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zamakhshari records variant vocalizations of لا نسقي, يصدر, and الرعاء.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( لا نسقي ) و ( يصدر ) . و ( الرعاء ) بضم النون والياء والراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الرعاء is a collective noun like الرخال and الثناء; the kasra vocalization follows the regular pattern of صيام and قيام.
rows.anchor: والرعاء : اسم جمع كالرخال والثناء . وأما الرعاء بالكسر فقياس ، كصيام وقيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كبير means advanced in age.
rows.anchor: { كبير } كبير السن { فسقى لهما } فسقى غنمهما لأجلهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objects of these verbs are omitted because the actions of watering and holding back matter, regardless of what was watered or held back.
rows.anchor: قلت : لأن الغرض هو الفعل لا المفعول . ألا ترى أنه إنما رحمهما لأنهما كانتا على الذياد وهم على السقي .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their answer explains that, as two weak, modest women without a man to help and with an aged father, they must wait until the men finish watering.
rows.anchor: قلت : سألهما عن سبب الذود فقالتا : السبب في ذلك أنا امرأتاه ضعيفتان مستورتان لا نقدر على مساجلة الرجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuayb's daughters tending livestock was not forbidden by religion; social standards vary across peoples, Bedouin and settled communities, especially in necessity.
rows.anchor: قلت : الأمر في نفسه ليس بمحظور ، فالدين لا يأباه . وأما المروأة ، فالناس مختلفون في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses says he needs whatever good God sends him, little or much, humble or plentiful.
rows.anchor: { إني } لأي شيء { أنزلت إلى } قليل أو كثير ، غث أو سمين ل { فقير } وإنما عدي فقير باللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فقير takes ل because the word includes the sense of a supplicant or seeker.
rows.anchor: وإنما عدي فقير باللام ؛ لأنه ضمن معنى سائل وطالب .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed report says hunger had made the green of plants visible through Moses' belly and that he asked God only for a meal.
rows.anchor: ما سأل الله إلا أكلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible reading is that Moses was poor in worldly goods because of the religious good of rescue from oppressors; he had been wealthy under Pharaoh and gives thanks for the better exchange.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد : إني فقير من الدنيا لأجل ما أنزلت إلي من خير الدين وهو النجاة من الظالمين .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shade where Moses sat was an acacia tree.
rows.anchor: وكان الظل ظل سمرة { على استحياء }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: على استحياء is circumstantial: she came shy and modest.
rows.anchor: { على استحياء } في موضع الحال ، أي : مستحيية متخفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed view says she covered herself with the sleeve of her dress.
rows.anchor: وقيل . قد استترت بكم درعها .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the daughters returned before the crowd with full flocks, told their father a compassionate righteous man had watered for them, and he sent one to invite Moses; wind pressed her garment against her body, so he asked her to walk ahead and describe the way, then reassured her that Pharaoh had no authority in their land.
rows.anchor: روي أنهما لما رجعتا إلى أبيهما قبل الناس وأغنامهما حفل بطان قال لهما : ما أعجلكما ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses could accept the woman's report as he would that of any free or enslaved person, male or female; she only relayed her father's invitation.
rows.anchor: فكما يعمل بقول الواحد حرا كان أو عبدا ذكرا كان أو أنثى في الأخبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Walking with an unrelated woman is permissible in a comparable situation when accompanied by caution and scrupulous conduct.
rows.anchor: وأما مما شاته امرأة أجنبية فلا بأس بها في نظائر تلك الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that Moses watered them solely for God's sake as an act of kindness.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون قد فعل ذلك لوجه الله وعلى سبيل البر والمعروف .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative says Shuaib's food and hospitality were a welcome gift, not payment; Moses' prophetic family deserved generous hosting, though poverty could also make earning wages permissible.
rows.anchor: وقيل إطعام شعيب وإحسانه لا على سبيل أخذ الأجر ، ولكن على سبيل التقبل لمعروف مبتدإ .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking wages for work is also permissible when poverty and need make earning necessary.
rows.anchor: وليس بمنكر أن يفعل ذلك لاضطرار الفقر والفاقة طلبا للأجر .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Moses disliked being told he would be rewarded and initially refused food until Shuaib explained that hospitality was his family's custom with every guest.
rows.anchor: روي أنها لما قالت : ليجزيك ، كره ذلك ، ولما قدم إليه الطعام امتنع وقال : إنا أهل بيت

rows.speaker: عطاء ابن السائب
rows.claim: Ataa ibn al-Saib says Moses raised his prayer so the women could hear him; hence أجر means compensation for his watering.
rows.anchor: وعن عطاء ابن السائب : رفع صوته بدعائه ليسمعهما ، فلذلك قيل له : ليجزيك أجر ما سقيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: القصص is a verbal noun like العلل, used here for the narrated story.
rows.anchor: والقصص : مصدر كالعلل ، سمي به المقصوص .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The elder daughter was called Safra and the younger Sufayra; Safra brought Moses to her father, requested that he hire him, and became his wife.
rows.anchor: كبراهما : كانت تسمى صفراء ، والصغرى : صفيراء . وصفراء : هي التي ذهبت به

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Shuaib's jealousy led him to ask how his daughter knew Moses was strong and trustworthy; she cited his lifting the stone, drawing the bucket, lowering his gaze, and asking her to walk behind him.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : أن شعيبا أحفظته الغيرة فقال : وما علمك بقوته وأمانته ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The daughter's saying is a compact maxim: competence and trust together give an employer peace of mind and fulfill the purpose of hiring.
rows.anchor: كلام حكيم جامع لا يزاد عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase puts خير من استأجرت first because it is the focus; Zamakhshari cites a line with the same emphasis-driven order.
rows.anchor: ألا إن خير الناس حيا وهالكا … لسير ثقيف عندهم في السلاسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past tense signals something already tried and known; a proverb illustrates this use.
rows.anchor: وورود الفعل بلفظ الماضي للدلالة على أنه أمر قد جرب وعرف . ومنه قولهم : أهون ما أعملت لسان ممخ .

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud calls three people exceptionally discerning: Shuayb's daughter, the man who recognized Joseph's value, and Abu Bakr in choosing Umar.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه : أفرس الناس ثلاثة : بنت شعيب ، وصاحب يوسف ، في قوله : { عسى أن ينفعنا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Shuayb married Moses to Safra.
rows.anchor: روي أنه أنكحه صفراء .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative 'these two' indicates that Shuayb had other daughters as well.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { هاتين } فيه دليل على أنه كانت له غيرهما { تأجرنى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تأجرني can mean that you work for me, or that I give you a specified compensation.
rows.anchor: { تأجرنى } من أجرته إذا كنت له أجيرا ، كقولك : أبوته إذا كنت له أبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ثماني حجج can be parsed as a time adverbial or as an object, with shepherding understood as work for eight seasons.
rows.anchor: و { ثمانى حجج } ظرفه . أو من أجرته كذا ، إذا أثبته إياه .

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A prophetic condolence formula cited with the compensation sense says, 'May God reward you and show you mercy.'
rows.anchor: ومنه : تعزية رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 812 ) ( أجركم الله ورحمكم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuaib's words were a proposal and description of an intention, not a marriage contract; a contract would say 'I have married you.'
rows.anchor: لم يكن ذلك عقدا للنكاح ، ولكن مواعدة ومواصفة أمر قد عزم عليه ، ولو كان عقدا لقال : قد أنكحتك

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa disallows marriage in exchange for the husband serving his wife, since the husband is not property, but permits service by a slave or use of a house as property.
rows.anchor: ألا ترى إلى أبي حنيفة كيف منع أن يتزوج امرأة بأن يخدمها سنة وجوز أن يتزوجها بأن يخدمها عبده سنة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafii permits marriage in exchange for a specified service or work.
rows.anchor: وأما الشافعي : فقد جوز التزوج على الإجارة لبعض الأعمال والخدمة ، إذا كان المستأجر له أو المخدوم فيه أمرا معلوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zamakhshari offers alternatives: the arrangement may have been lawful under Shuayb's dispensation, the dowry may have been separate, or shepherding and marriage may have been linked as a pact rather than a contract.
rows.anchor: ولعل ذلك كان جائزا في تلك الشريعة . ويجوز أن يكون المهر شيئا آخر ، وإنما أراد أن يكون راعي غنمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is that Moses was hired for eight years at a known wage, paid, and then married to the daughter with the wage as dowry; the phrase summarizes their agreement.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يستأجره لرعية ثماني سنين بمبلغ معلوم ويوفيه إياه ، ثم ينكحه ابنته به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Moses completes ten years, the extra two are a voluntary favor from him, not an obligation imposed by Shuayb.
rows.anchor: لا ألزمكه ولا أحتمه عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuayb will not force Moses to complete the longer term; more broadly, he promises not to overburden him as hard employers do by nitpicking time and work.
rows.anchor: { وما أريد أن أشق عليك } بإلزام أتم الأجلين وإيجابه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image of hardship is that a daunting task seems to split one's judgment between thinking it bearable and unbearable.
rows.anchor: حقيقته أن الأمر إذا تعاظمك فكأنه شق عليك ظنك باثنين ، تقول تارة : أطيقه ، وتارة : لا أطيقه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuayb also promises lenient treatment and no unreasonable scrutiny or extra duties; prophets choose the gentlest course in people's dealings.
rows.anchor: ولا يفعل نحو ما يفعل المعاسرون من المسترعين ، من المناقشة في مراعاة الأوقات

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A prophetic report says, 'He was my partner, and a good partner: he did not evade, haggle, or argue,' illustrating fair partnership.
rows.anchor: ( 813 ) ( كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم شريكي ، فكان خير شريك لا يداري ولا يشاري ولا يماري )

words: ستجدني إن شاء الله من الصالحين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الصالحين may mean good conduct, agreeable character, and gentleness, or righteousness in general, which includes good dealings.
rows.anchor: يريد بالصلاح : حسن المعاملة ووطأة الخلق ولين الجانب . ويجوز أن يريد الصلاح على العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning God's will expresses reliance on His guidance and help, not uncertainty about whether Shuayb will behave well.
rows.anchor: والمراد باشتراط مشيئة الله بما وعد من الصلاح : الاتكال على توفيقه فيه ومعونته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذلك is the subject and بيني وبينك its predicate; the phrase points to their mutual agreement, binding each to his terms.
rows.anchor: { ذالك } مبتدأ ، و { بينى وبينك } خبره ، وهو إشارة إلى ما عاهده عليه شعيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whichever term Moses completes, eight or ten, no further work may be demanded; the two choices are equally established, and extra years remain voluntary.
rows.anchor: أي أجل من الأجلين قضيت : أطولهما الذي هو العشر ، أو أقصرهما الذي هو الثمان { فلا عدوان على }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes the phrase as Moses denying wrongdoing by himself, like saying, 'No sin or liability is on me.'
rows.anchor: وقيل : معناه فلا أكون متعديا ، وهو في نفي العدوان عن نفسه ، كقولك : لا إثم علي

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud's reading is أي الأجلين ما قضيت; another reading vocalizes أيما with a still yāʾ, as illustrated by a poetic question about which of two signs brings rain.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة ابن مسعود : أي الأجلين ما قضيت . وقرىء : ( أيما ) بسكون الياء ، كقوله

rows.speaker: ابن قطيب
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba records a reading with the dāl of عدوان vocalized with kasra.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن قطيب : عدوان ، بالكسر .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the common reading, added ما emphasizes the breadth of the choice; in the anomalous reading it emphasizes the firmness of the term Moses resolves to complete.
rows.anchor: وقعت في المستفيضة مؤكدة لإبهام ، أي : زائدة في شياعها : وفي الشاذة تأكيدا للقضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الوكيل is one entrusted with a matter; the word also means witness, overseer, or sustainer, explaining the preposition على.
rows.anchor: الوكيل : الذي وكل إليه الأمر ، ولما استعمل في موضع الشاهد والمهيمن والمقيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says Shuayb kept the prophets' staff, which Adam brought from Paradise and the prophets inherited; Moses selected it repeatedly, and Shuayb recognized its importance when it came to Moses seven times.
rows.anchor: روي أن شعيبا كانت عنده عصى الأنبياء فقال لموسى بالليل : ادخل ذلك البيت فخذ عصا من تلك العصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says Gabriel took the staff after Adam and kept it until he met Moses with it at night.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أخذها جبريل بعد موت آدم فكانت معه حتى لقي بها موسى ليلا .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further story says an angel entrusted the staff to Shuayb, whose daughter brought it seven times; Shuayb regretted giving it away, but Moses lifted it in a test of ownership.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أودعها شعيبا ملك في صورة رجل ، فأمر بنته أن تأتيه بعصا ، فأتته بها فردها سبع مرات

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says Moses' staff was simply a stick he picked from a tree.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن : ما كانت إلا عصا من الشجر اعترضها اعتراضا .

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi identifies the tree as al-ʿawsaj, the thorn bush from which Moses was called.
rows.anchor: وعن الكلبي : الشجرة التي منها نودي شجرة العوسج ، ومنها كانت عصاه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A journey report says Shuayb warned Moses away from a fork with dangerous dragons; the sheep went right, where Moses found rich pasture, and his staff killed an attacking dragon. Shuayb promised marked-color lambs, later fulfilled after God instructed Moses to strike the watering trough.
rows.anchor: ولما أصبح قال له شعيب : إذا بلغت مفرق الطريق فلا تأخذ على يمينك ، فإن الكلأ وإن كان بها أكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whatever worldly means people receive is only brief enjoyment and adornment for a finite life; God's reward is better and lasts forever.
rows.anchor: وأي شيء أصبتموه من أسباب الدنيا فما هو إلا تمتع وزينة أياما قلائل ، وهي مدة الحياة المتقضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with third-person يَعقلون is more forceful as a warning.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( يعقلون ) بالياء ، وهو أبلغ في الموعظة .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says God made three classes in the world: believers provision for the next life, hypocrites adorn themselves, and disbelievers simply enjoy worldly life.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن الله خلق الدنيا وجعل أهلها ثلاثة أصناف : المؤمن ، والمنافق ، والكافر
